# The ;af3aal_quloob;

;wip_warn;

## Introduction

Consider the sentence:

(@) [زَيْدٌ قَائِمٌ]{.ar}  
    [Zayd is standing.]{.trans}  

This entire sentence can be the inner sentence of a compound sentence as the ;mafulb; of the verb
[قَالَ]{.ar}.
So we can say:

(@) [قُلْتُ زَيْدٌ قَائِمٌ]{.ar}  
    [I said, "Zayd is standing."]{.trans}  

In example () above, the verb
[قَالَ]{.ar}
does not exercise its ;3amal; _within_ the inner sentence
[زَيْدٌ قَائِمٌ]{.ar}.
Rather, the inner sentence is,
as a whole,
the (;mahall;) ;mafulb;.
This is because the verb
[قَالَ]{.ar}
does not have a meaningful connection with the
_content_ of the inner sentence.
It is simply relating the sentence as direct speech.

In addition to a ;j_ism; like
[زَيْدٌ قَائِمٌ]{.ar},
a ;j_f3l; too can be the ;mafulb; of
[قَالَ]{.ar}.
So, for example,
we can say:

(@) [قُلْتُ ضَرَبَ زَيْدٌ]{.ar}
    [@radiy_kafiyah@]{.citex}  
    [I said, "Zayd beat."]{.trans}  

Now let's consider what happens when a
;j_ism; is made the ;mafulb; of a class of verbs
called _;af3aal_quloob;_.

_#;af3aal_quloob;_ are a class
of verbs that signify actions taking place within the mind.
Some examples of ;af3aal_quloob; are:

+ [ظَنَّ]{.ar} [to conjecture, assume]{.trans}
+ [عَلِمَ]{.ar} [to know]{.trans}
+ [حَسِبَ]{.ar} [to deem]{.trans}
+ [خَالَ]{.ar} [to imagine]{.trans}

These verbs can take a inner ;j_ism;
as a ;mafulb;,
but instead of taking the entire inner sentence as one ;mafulb;,
the ;fi3l_qalb;
exercises its ;3amal; within the inner sentence
and ;3amil;s the
original ;mubtada; and ;xabar; of the inner sentence individually
as two ;mafulb;s.
For example:

(@) [ظَنَنْتُ زَيْدًا قَائِمًا]{.ar}  
    [I assumed Zayd to be standing.]{.trans}  

Note that 
[زَيْدًا]{.ar}
and
[قَائِمًا]{.ar}
are both in the ;acase;
because they are,
individually,
the ;mafulb;s of ;dhanna;.
The verb ;dhanna;
is able to break up the original
;j_ism;
[زَيْدٌ قَائِمٌ]{.ar}
and ;3amil; its constituents individually
because it has a meaningful connection with the
content of the inner sentence.
This is because
the original ;mubtada; ([زَيْد]{.ar})'s relationship with
the original ;xabar; ([قَائِم]{.ar})
is only established via the meaning of the verb ;dhanna;.
That is,
the sentence
in example () above
is not saying that Zayd is standing.
Rather it is saying that _I thought_ Zayd to be standing.
So Zayd's "standing-ness" is only established via my assumption of it.

The ;fi3l_qalb; thus describes the
nature of speaker's belief
of the actuality of the
original
;xabar;
ocurring from the original ;mubtada;.^[[@radiy_kafiyah@ 4/153](https://ketabonline.com/ar/books/23090/read?page=1588&part=4#p-23090-1588-2)]

So, for example,
[ظَنَنْتُ زَيْدًا قَائِمًا]{.ar}
signifies my _assumption_ of Zayd's standing.
And
[عَلِمْتُ زَيْدًا قَائِمًا]{.ar}
signifies my _knowledge_ of Zayd's standing.


## The ;isnaad; of the ;fi3l_qalb; sentence

The basic ;j_ism; consists of a ;mubtada; and a ;xabar;.
For example:

(@) [زَيْدٌ أَخُوكَ]{.ar}  
    [Zayd is your brother.]{.trans}  

In example () above,
[زَيْدٌ]{.ar}
is the ;mubtada;
and
[أَخُوكَ]{.ar}
is its ;xabar;.
Both are in the ;ucase; because it is a basic ;j_ism;.
In terms of its ;isnaad;,
[زَيْدٌ]{.ar}
is the ;musnadi;
and
[أَخُوكَ]{.ar}
is the ;musnad;.
(Technically, the ;musnad; is [أَخ]{.ar}. And it in turn is a ;mudaf; to the ;mudafil; [كَ]{.ar}.
But loosely speaking, we can say that the ;musnad; is the bundled [أَخُوكَ]{.ar}.)
With the ;musnadi; and the ;musnad; in place, the sentence is ;isnaad_comp;.

Now consider the following sentence:

(@) [ظَنَنْتُ زَيْدًا أَخَاكَ]{.ar}
    [@peled_sentence_types@ 188]{.citex}  
    [I thought Zayd to be your brother.]{.trans}  

In example () above,
the verb ;dhanna;
takes the ;mubtada; and ;xabar; of example (),
and makes them into ;mafulb;s.
The verb ;dhanna;
requires a ;faa3il; (as usual),
which is the pronoun [تُ]{.ar} [I]{.trans}.
And it also requires two ;mafulb;s:
[زَيْدًا]{.ar}
is the first ;mafulb;
and
[أَخَاكَ]{.ar}
is the second ;mafulb;.

This sentence is peculiar in its ;isnaad;.
This is because the ;3umdah; elements are the two ;mafulb;s.
[زَيْدًا]{.ar}
is the ;musnadi;
and
[أَخَاكَ]{.ar}
is the ;musnad;.^[[@baseet_ibn_abi_rabee3@ 433](https://archive.org/details/0969pdf_201912/page/n432/mode/1up)]
The sentence is only ;isnaad_comp; when both ;mafulb;s are in place.
The sentence may still be categorized as a ;j_f3l;.
However, unlike normal ;j_f3l;s,
the verb ;dhanna; and its ;faa3il; are not the ;3umdah; elements of the sentence.
Rather ;dhanna; is the ;pregov;.
Figure () depicts the ;3amal; of example ().

Parallels of the ;isnaad; of the ;dhanna; sentence
may be found in the ;kaana; and ;inna; sentences:

(@) [كَانَ زَيْدٌ أَخَاكَ]{.ar}
    [@peled_sentence_types@ 188]{.citex}  
    [Zayd was your brother.]{.trans}  
    ([زَيْدٌ]{.ar}, the ;faa3il;/;ism_of;, is the ;musnadi;.
    [أَخَاكَ]{.ar}, the ;mafulb;/;xabar;, is the ;musnad;.
    ;kaana; is the ;pregov;.)


(@) [إِنَّ زَيْدًا أَخُوكَ]{.ar}
    [@peled_sentence_types@ 188]{.citex}  
    [Indeed Zayd is your brother.]{.trans}  
    ([زَيْدًا]{.ar}, the ;ism_of;, is the ;musnadi;.
    [أَخُوكَ]{.ar}, the ;xabar;, is the ;musnad;.
    ;inna; is the ;pregov;.)

the verb and its ;faa3il; don't make the sentence ;isnaad_comp;.

## The ;af3aal_quloob; as ;passive; verbs

When ;af3aal_quloob; are used in the passive voice,
the first ;mafulb;
(the one which is the ;mubtada; in the basic ;j_ism;)
is made the ;naib_faa3il; in the ;ucase;.
And the second ;mafulb;
(the one which is the ;xabar; in the basic ;j_ism;)
remains a ;mafulb; in the ;acase;.
So, example () above, becomes in the passive voice:

(@) [ظُنَّ زَيْدٌ أَخَاكَ]{.ar}  
    [Zayd was thought to be your brother.]{.trans}

Similarly,

(@) [زَيْدٌ مَظْنُونٌ شُجَاعًا]{.ar}
    [@wright@ 2/52D]{.citex}  
    [Zayd is thought to be brave.]{.trans}  


## ;anna; and ;an; with ;af3aal_quloob;

Consider again the sentence:

(@) [ظَنَنْتُ زَيْدًا قَائِمًا]{.ar}  
    [I assumed Zayd to be standing.]{.trans}  

Literally
[زَيْدًا]{.ar}
and
[قَائِمًا]{.ar}
are both,
individually,
the ;mafulb;s of ;dhanna;.
However,
in terms of meaning,
the ;taqdir; of the sentence is:

(@) [ظَنَنْتُ قِيَامَ زَيْدٍ]{.ar}  
    [I assumed Zayd to be standing.]{.trans}  

That is,
in the ;taqdir; of the sentence,
;dhanna; has one ;mafulb; which is the
;masdar;
([قِيَام]{.ar})
of the second ;mafulb;
([قَائِم]{.ar})
;yudaaf;ed to the first ;mafulb;
([زَيْد]{.ar}).

We have seen
;masdar;s as a ;taqdir; before
in the analysis of
;anna; and ;an;.
And this similarity allows
;anna; and ;an; (with their clauses)
to optionally occur as the ;mafulb; of ;af3aal_quloob;.^[@radiy_kafiyah@; @nahw_wafi@ 2/43]
So instead of saying
[ظَنَنْتُ زَيْدًا قَائِمًا]{.ar},
we can instead say:

(@) [ظَنَنْتُ **أَنَّ** زَيْدًا قَائِمٌ]{.ar}  
    [I assumed **that** Zayd is standing.]{.trans}  

or:

(@) [ظَنَنْتُ **أَنْ** يَقُومَ زَيْدٌ]{.ar}  
    [I assumed **that** Zayd would stand.]{.trans}  

Now the ;anna; and ;an; clauses, respectively,
are, formally,
the single ;mafulb; of ;dhanna;.
This substitution of the two ;mafulb;s
of ;af3aal_quloob;
can be considered a form of _;ta3leeq;_,^[[@utheymeen_alfiyyah@ 28/3](https://shamela.ws/book/36954/273); [@haazimi@ 43/2](https://shamela.ws/book/36130/789)]
but is really more basic than it.
We will study ;ta3leeq; in @sec-ta3leeq below, ;ia;.

In terms of meaning,
example () above is more assertive than
the original example ().
Whereas,
example () is less assertive and more doubtful than
the original example ().

Here is another example of substituting the
;mafulb;s of a ;fi3l_qalb;
with an ;anna; clause:

(@) [عَلِمْتُ زَيْدًا قَائِمًا]{.ar}  
    [I knew Zayd to be standing.]{.trans}  

(@) [عَلِمْتُ **أَنَّ** زَيْدًا قَائِمٌ]{.ar}  
    [I knew **that** Zayd is standing.]{.trans}  

In this case, we will only use ;anna;
and not ;an;
because,
as we learned in section\ (),
only ;anna; is used in cases of certainty,
which is what the verb [عَلِمَ]{.ar} implies.

In examples () and (),
it was easy to come up with a ;masdari; equivalence of the
two ;mafulb;s of the ;af3aal_quloob;.
This is because the second ;mafulb;
([قَائِم]{.ar})
was a ;mushtaqq; noun.
But what if the
the second ;mafulb; was a ;jamid_noun;?
For example:

(@) [عَلِمْتُ أَخَاكَ زَيْدًا]{.ar}
    [[@radiy_kafiyah@ 3/152](https://ketabonline.com/ar/books/23090/read?page=1587&part=4#p-23090-1587-2)]{.citex}  
    [I knew your brother to be Zayd.]{.trans}  

In this case we can manufacture a ;masdar; from the ;jamid_noun;,
and still retain the ;taqdir;, thus:

(@) [عَلِمْتُ **زَيْدِيَّةَ** أَخِيكَ]{.ar}
    [[@radiy_kafiyah@ 3/152](https://ketabonline.com/ar/books/23090/read?page=1587&part=4#p-23090-1587-2)]{.citex}  
    [I knew the **Zayd-ness** of your brother.]{.trans}  

And using this ;masdari; equivalence,
we can substitute it with ;anna;, thus:

(@) [عَلِمْتُ **أَنَّ** أَخَاكَ زَيْدٌ]{.ar}  
    [I knew **that** your brother is Zayd.]{.trans}

;dhanna; is one of these verbs.
For example:

(@) [ظَنَنْتُ زَيْدًا أَخَاكَ]{.ar}

## The verbs that comprise the ;af3aal_quloob;

### ;dhanna;

;dhanna; is the typical ;fi3l_qalb;.
Its basic meaning is 
[to conjecture]{.trans}
or
[to assume]{.trans}.
But it (and the ;af3aal_quloob; in general)
can often be translated as
[to think]{.trans}.

;dhanna;
can be used in a range of circumstances from
situations
where its ;faa3il; believes something to be certain,
to cases where he is doubtful.
Here are some examples:

(@) [وَإِنِّی لَأَظُنُّكَ یَـٰفِرۡعَوۡنُ مَثۡبُورࣰا]{.quran}
    [@https://quran.com/17/102@ cited by @nahw_arabi@ 1/331]{.citex}  
    [and indeed I think, O Pharaoh, that you are destroyed.]{.trans}  

(@) [قُلۡتُم مَّا نَدۡرِی مَا ٱلسَّاعَةُ إِن نَّظُنُّ إِلَّا ظَنࣰّا وَمَا نَحۡنُ بِمُسۡتَیۡقِنِینَ]{.quran}
    [@https://quran.com/45/32@ cited by @nahw_arabi@ 1/331]{.citex}  
    [you said, 'We know not what is the Hour. We assume only assumption, and we are not convinced.']{.trans}  

(@) [ظَنَنْتُكَ إِنْ شَبَّتْ لَظَى الْحَرْبِ صَالِيًا]{.ar}
    [cited by @nahw_arabi@ 1/331]{.citex}  
    [I thought you, if the blaze of war is kindled, to be entering (therein)]{.trans}  

;dhanna; following examples is interpreted to have certainty in its meaning:

(@) [قَالَ ٱلَّذِینَ یَظُنُّونَ أَنَّهُم مُّلَـٰقُوا۟ ٱللَّهِ كَم مِّن فِئَةࣲ قَلِیلَةٍ غَلَبَتۡ فِئَةࣰ كَثِیرَةَۢ بِإِذۡنِ ٱللَّهِۗ وَٱللَّهُ مَعَ ٱلصَّـٰبِرِینَ]{.quran}^[See @https://tafsir.app/ibn-uthaymeen/2/249@]
    [@https://quran.com/2/249@ cited by @nahw_arabi@ 1/332]{.citex}  
    [But those who were certain that they would meet Allāh said, "How many a small company has overcome a large company by permission of Allāh. And Allāh is with the patient."]{.trans}

(@) [إِنِّی ظَنَنتُ أَنِّی مُلَـٰقٍ حِسَابِیَهۡ]{.quran}
    [@https://quran.com/69/20@ cited by @nahw_arabi@ 1/332]{.citex}  
    [Indeed, I was certain that I would be meeting my account."]{.trans}  

(@) [وَرَءَا ٱلۡمُجۡرِمُونَ ٱلنَّارَ فَظَنُّوۤا۟ أَنَّهُم مُّوَاقِعُوهَا وَلَمۡ یَجِدُوا۟ عَنۡهَا مَصۡرِفࣰا]{.quran}^[See @https://tafsir.app/ibn-uthaymeen/18/53@]
    [@https://quran.com/18/53@ cited by @nahw_arabi@ 1/332]{.citex}  
    [And the criminals will see the Fire and will be certain that they are to fall therein. And they will not find from it a way elsewhere.]{.trans}  

;dhanna; can be used with both ;anna;
(as above)
and the ;naasib; ;an;.
Here is an example with the ;naasib; ;an;:

(@) [تَظُنُّ **أَن** یُفۡعَلَ بِهَا فَاقِرَةࣱ]{.quran}
    [@https://quran.com/75/25@]{.citex}

Even so, example () above is interpreted to have certitude,
or at least a preponderance of belief,
in its
meaning.^[@https://tafsir.app/albahr-almuheet/75/25@]

The ;muxaffaf; ;an; can also be used.
For example:

(@) [وَظَنُّوۤا۟ **أَن** لَّا مَلۡجَأَ مِنَ ٱللَّهِ إِلَّاۤ إِلَیۡهِ]{.quran}
    [@https://quran.com/9/118@]{.citex}  

;an; in example () above is interpreted to be
the ;muxaffaf; ;an;.^[@https://tafsir.app/aldur-almasoon/9/118@]

Sometimes ;dhanna;
can have a specialized meaning
[to suspect]{.trans}.
In this case, it no longer needs two ;mafulb;s,
and will take only one ;mafulb;.
For example:

(@) [ظَنَّ القَاضِي فُلَانًا]{.ar}
    [@nahw_arabi@ 1/331]{.citex}  
    [The judge suspected so-and-so.]{.trans}  

(@) [عُدِمَ لِي مَالٌ فَظَنَنْتُ زَيْدًا]{.ar}
    [[@howell@ §442 2/150](https://adamiturabi.github.io/howell-navigator/content/2-07-0.html?page=211)]{.citex}  
    [Some property of mine was missing so I suspected Zayd.]{.trans}  

### [عَلِمَ]{.ar}

[عَلِمَ]{.ar}
means
[to know]{.trans}.
Here are some examples of its usage:

(@) [عَلِمْتُكَ الْبَاذِلَ الْمَعْرُوفَ]{.ar}
    [@wright@ 2/49B]{.citex}  
    [I have known you to be liberal in the exercise of bounty.]{.trans}  

(@) [فَإِنۡ **عَلِمۡتُمُوهُنَّ مُؤۡمِنَـٰتࣲ** فَلَا تَرۡجِعُوهُنَّ إِلَى ٱلۡكُفَّارِۖ]{.quran}
    [@https://quran.com/60/10@ cited by @nahw_arabi@ 1/325]{.citex}  
    [And if **you know them to be believers**, then do not return them to the disbelievers;]{.trans}  

(@) [عَنِ ابْنِ عَبَّاسٍ، وَالْحَسَنِ بْنِ عَلِيٍّ ، مَرَّتْ بِهِمَا جَنَازَةٌ فَقَامَ أَحَدُهُمَا وَقَعَدَ الآخَرُ فَقَالَ الَّذِي قَامَ أَمَا وَاللَّهِ لَقَدْ **عَلِمْتُ أَنَّ** رَسُولَ اللَّهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم قَدْ قَامَ قَالَ لَهُ الَّذِي جَلَسَ لَقَدْ **عَلِمْتُ أَنَّ** رَسُولَ اللَّهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم قَدْ جَلَسَ]{.ar}
    [@https://sunnah.com/nasai:1926@]{.citex}  
    [[It was narrated] from Ibn [#eabbAs]{.trn2} and [al-#Hasan ibn #ealiyy]{.trn2}: A funeral passed by them and one of them stood and the other [stayed] seated. The one who stood up said, "By ;Allah;, **I know that** the Messenger of ;Allah; ;pbuh; had stood up." The one who [stayed] seated said to him, "Indeed **I know that** the Messenger of ;Allah; ;pbuh; had [stayed] seated."]{.trans}

(@) [إِنَّ رَبَّكَ **یَعۡلَمُ أَنَّكَ تَقُومُ** أَدۡنَىٰ مِن ثُلُثَیِ ٱلَّیۡلِ وَنِصۡفَهُۥ وَثُلُثَهُۥ وَطَاۤىِٕفَةࣱ مِّنَ ٱلَّذِینَ مَعَكَۚ وَٱللَّهُ یُقَدِّرُ ٱلَّیۡلَ وَٱلنَّهَارَۚ **عَلِمَ أَن لَّن تُحۡصُوهُ** فَتَابَ عَلَیۡكُمۡۖ فَٱقۡرَءُوا۟ مَا تَیَسَّرَ مِنَ ٱلۡقُرۡءَانِۚ **عَلِمَ أَن سَیَكُونُ مِنكُم مَّرۡضَىٰ** وَءَاخَرُونَ یَضۡرِبُونَ فِی ٱلۡأَرۡضِ یَبۡتَغُونَ مِن فَضۡلِ ٱللَّهِ وَءَاخَرُونَ یُقَـٰتِلُونَ فِی سَبِیلِ ٱللَّهِۖ فَٱقۡرَءُوا۟ مَا تَیَسَّرَ مِنۡهُۚ وَأَقِیمُوا۟ ٱلصَّلَوٰةَ وَءَاتُوا۟ ٱلزَّكَوٰةَ وَأَقۡرِضُوا۟ ٱللَّهَ قَرۡضًا حَسَنࣰاۚ وَمَا تُقَدِّمُوا۟ لِأَنفُسِكُم مِّنۡ خَیۡرࣲ تَجِدُوهُ عِندَ ٱللَّهِ هُوَ خَیۡرࣰا وَأَعۡظَمَ أَجۡرࣰاۚ وَٱسۡتَغۡفِرُوا۟ ٱللَّهَۖ إِنَّ ٱللَّهَ غَفُورࣱ رَّحِیمُۢ]{.quran}
    [@https://quran.com/73/20@]{.citex}  
    [Indeed, **your Lord knows, [O Muḥammad], that you stand [in prayer]** almost two thirds of the night or half of it or a third of it, and [so do] a group of those with you. And Allāh determines [the extent of] the night and the day. **He has known that you [Muslims] will not be able to do it** and has turned to you in forgiveness, so recite what is easy [for you] of the Qur’ān. **He has known that there will be among you those who are ill** and others traveling throughout the land seeking [something] of the bounty of Allāh and others fighting for the cause of Allāh. So recite what is easy from it and establish prayer and give zakāh and loan Allāh a goodly loan. And whatever good you put forward for yourselves - you will find it with Allāh. It is better and greater in reward. And seek forgiveness of Allāh. Indeed, Allāh is Forgiving and Merciful.]{.trans}  
    (;an; in [أَنْ لَنْ]{.ar} and [أَنْ سيكونُ]{.ar} is the ;muxaffaf; ;an;,^[@https://tafsir.app/aldur-almasoon/73/20@] whose ;ism_of; is a ;mahzoof; ;damir_shan;.^[@https://tafsir.app/iraab-aldarweesh/73/20@])  

<!--
[عَلِمَ]{.ar}
is special in that it can take only one ;mafulb;,
even without ;anna;,
while retaining its meaning as a ;fi3l_qalb;.^[@radiy_kafiyah_imam@ 2/988]
For example:

(@) [عَلِمْتُ زَيْدًا]{.ar}
    [@radiy_kafiyah_imam@ 2/988]{.citex}  
    [I knew Zayd.]{.trans}  

(@) [عَلِمْتُ خُرُوجَ زَيْدٍ]{.ar}
    [@radiy_kafiyah_imam@ 2/988]{.citex}  
    [I knew Zayd's going out.]{.trans}  

Example () above
does not even require a ;masdari; meaning in order to take one ;mafulb;.
-->

### [رَأَى]{.ar}

[رَأَى]{.ar},
as a sensory verb,
means
[to see]{.trans} with the eye.
As such, it will typically take
one ;mafulb;.
For example:

(@) [رَأَيْتُهُ]{.ar}
    [[@howell@ §442 2/150](https://adamiturabi.github.io/howell-navigator/content/2-07-0.html?page=211)]{.citex}  
    [I saw him]{.trans}  

When [رَأَىٰ]{.ar} has this sensory meaning,
then there may be a second ;acase; (indefinite) ;ma3mul; as a ;haal;.^[@baseet_ibn_abi_rabee3@ 445]
For example:

(@) [رَأَيْتُ زَيْدًا ضَاحِكًا]{.ar}
    [@baseet_ibn_abi_rabee3@ 445]{.citex}  
    [I saw Zayd laughing.]{.trans}  

[رَأَىٰ]{.ar}
can also mean
[to hold (an opinion)]{.trans}.
In this case as well, it will take one ;mafulb;.
For example:

(@) [رَأَىٰ أَبُو حَنِيفَةَ حِلَّ كَذَا]{.ar}
    [[@howell@ §442 2/150](https://adamiturabi.github.io/howell-navigator/content/2-07-0.html?page=211)]{.citex}  
    [[#abU #HanIfah]{.trn2} held (the opinion of) the lawfulness of such a thing.]{.trans}

As a ;fi3l_qalb;,
[رَأَى]{.ar}
means
[to regard]{.trans} in the mind.
It may still be translated as
[to see]{.trans},
but this "seeing" is with the mind.
Now
[رَأَى]{.ar}
will take take two ;mafulb;s.

Here are some examples of
[رَأَى]{.ar}:

(@) [رَأَيْتُ اللهَ أَكْبَرَ كُلِّ شَيْءٍ مُحَاوَلَةً وَأَكْثَرُهُمْ جُنُودًا]{.ar}
    [[@howell@ §440 2/134](https://adamiturabi.github.io/howell-navigator/content/2-07-0.html?page=195)]{.citex}  
    [I regarded ;Allah; as the greatest of eveything in resource, and the most numerous of them in hosts.]{.trans}  

(@) [إِنَّهُمۡ یَرَوۡنَهُۥ بَعِیدࣰا۝ وَنَرَىٰهُ قَرِیبࣰا۝]{.quran}
    [@https://quran.com/70/6-7@]{.citex}  
    [Indeed, they see it [as] distant, But We see it [as] near.]{.trans}

Even when
[رَأَى]{.ar}
contains the meaning of a sensory verb,
it can still take two ;mafulb;s
when the mind takes what it sees
and regards it to be something.^[See @baseet_ibn_abi_rabee3@ 447; [@ibn_malik_sharh_tasheel@ 2/327](https://shamela.ws/book/13257/723); @https://tafsir.app/aldur-almasoon/12/4@; [@radiy_kafiyah@ 4/151](https://ketabonline.com/ar/books/23090/read?page=1586&part=4#p-23090-1586-2)]
For example:

(@) [يَا مَعْشَرَ النِّسَاءِ تَصَدَّقْنَ وَأَكْثِرْنَ فَإِنِّي **رَأَيْتُكُنَّ أَكْثَرَ أَهْلِ النَّارِ** لِكَثْرَةِ اللَّعْنِ وَكُفْرِ الْعَشِيرِ]{.ar}
    [@https://hadithunlocked.com/ahmad:5343@ cited by @baseet_ibn_abi_rabee3@ 447 footnote 1]{.citex}  
    [O women, give charity and do a lot of it, for indeed **I saw you to be the majority of the people of the Fire**, because of much cursing [on your part] and being ungrateful to the husband.]{.trans}  

(@) [رَأَیۡتُهُمۡ لِی سَـٰجِدِینَ]{.quran}
    [@https://quran.com/12/4@ cited by [@radiy_kafiyah@ 4/151](https://ketabonline.com/ar/books/23090/read?page=1586&part=4#p-23090-1586-2)]{.citex}  
    [I saw them prostrating to me.]{.trans}  

### [حَسِبَ]{.ar}

[حَسِبَ]{.ar} means [to deem]{.trans}.
As with ;dhanna;,
it can be translated with the verb [think]{.trans}.
Here are some examples:

(@) [حَسِبْتُ التُّقَىٰ وَالْجُودَ خَيْرَ تِجَارَةٍ رَبَاحًا]{.ar}
    [@wright@ 2/49C]{.citex}  
    [I deemed piety and generosity the best merchandise, in terms of profit.]{.trans}  

(@) [وَلَا تَحۡسَبَنَّ ٱلَّذِینَ قُتِلُوا۟ فِی سَبِیلِ ٱللَّهِ أَمۡوَ ٰ⁠تَۢاۚ]{.quran}
    [@https://quran.com/3/169@ cited by @wright@ 2/49C]{.citex}  
    [And never think of those who have been killed in the cause of Allāh as dead.]{.trans}  

(@) [صَنَعْنَا لِرَسُولِ اللهِ ﷺ فَخَّارَةً ، فَأَتَيْتُهُ بِهَا ، فَوَضَعْتُهَا بَيْنَ يَدَيْهِ ، فَاطَّلَعَ فِيهَا ، فَقَالَ : **حَسِبْتُهُ لَحْمًا**]{.ar}
    [@https://hadithunlocked.com/ahmad:14581@]{.citex}  
    [We made a (clay) pot (of food) for the Messenger of ;Allah; ;pbuh; and I brought it to him. He peered into it and said, "**I thought it was meat.**"]{.trans}  

(@) [أَحَسِبَ ٱلنَّاسُ **أَن یُتۡرَكُوۤا۟** أَن یَقُولُوۤا۟ ءَامَنَّا وَهُمۡ لَا یُفۡتَنُونَ]{.quran}
    [@https://quran.com/29/2@ cited by [@haazimi@ 43/2](https://shamela.ws/book/36130/789)]{.citex}  
    [Do the people think **that they will be left** to say, "We believe" and they will not be tried?]{.trans}  
    (The ;masdar; from [أَنْ يُتْرَكُوا]{.ar} ;sadd_masadd; of the two ;mafulb;s.^[[@haazimi@ 43/2](https://shamela.ws/book/36130/789); @https://tafsir.app/aldur-almasoon/29/2@])

### [وَجَدَ]{.ar}

[وَجَدَ]{.ar}
is also a sensory verb which means [to find]{.trans}.
When it is used to mean that the mind has found something to be another thing,
then it is used as a ;fi3l_qalb;
and can take two ;mafulb;s.
Examples:

(@) [وَإِن وَجَدۡنَاۤ أَكۡثَرَهُمۡ لَفَـٰسِقِینَ]{.quran}
    [@https://quran.com/7/102@ cited by [@ibn_aqil_alfiyyah@ 2/31](https://shamela.ws/book/9904/418)]{.citex}  
    [but indeed, We found most of them defiantly disobedient.]{.trans}  
    ([أَكْثَرَهُمْ]{.ar} and [لَفَاسِقِينَ]{.ar} are both analyzed to be ;mafulb;s.)  


(@) [كُنَّا مَعْشَرُ قُرَيْشٍ قَوْمًا نَغْلِبُ النِّسَاءَ فَلَمَّا قَدِمْنَا الْمَدِينَةَ **وَجَدْنَاهُمْ قَوْمًا** تَغْلِبُهُمْ نِسَاؤُهُمْ]{.ar}
    [@https://hadithunlocked.com/ibnhibban:4268a@]{.citex}  
    [We, the people of [#qurayc]{.trn2}, were a people who were dominant over the women. But when we came to [al-#madInah]{.trn2}, **we found them to be a people** whose women dominated them.]{.trans}  

As with
[رَأَى]{.ar},
when
[وَجَدَ]{.ar}
is used merely as a sensory verb,
then it will take only one ;mafulb;.
A second ;acase; noun with it will then be construed as a ;haal;.^[@wright@ 2/50C]
For example:

(@) [وَجَدْتُهُ **مَرِيضًا**]{.ar}
    [@wright@ 2/50C]{.citex}  
    [I found him **sick**.]{.trans}  
    ([مَرِيضًا]{.ar} is a ;haal;.)

Similarly:

(@) [أَلَمۡ یَجِدۡكَ **یَتِیمࣰا** فَـَٔاوَىٰ۝ وَوَجَدَكَ **ضَاۤلࣰّا** فَهَدَىٰ۝ وَوَجَدَكَ **عَاۤىِٕلࣰا** فَأَغۡنَىٰ۝]{.quran}
    [@https://quran.com/93/6-8@]{.citex}  
    [Did He not find you **an orphan** and give [you] refuge?  And He found you **lost** and guided [you], And He found you **poor** and made [you] self-sufficient.]{.trans}  
    ([يَتِيمًا]{.ar}, [ضَالًّا]{.ar}, and [عَائِلًا]{.ar} are analyzed as ;haal;s.^[@https://tafsir.app/ibn-aashoor/93/6@]. Although, a ;mafulb; interpretation for at least one of them also seems to be possible.^[@https://tafsir.app/iraab-aldarweesh/93/6@])  

### [خَالَ]{.ar}

[خَالَ]{.ar} means [to imagine or fancy (something)]{.trans}.
It too is often translated as [to think]{.trans}.
[خَالَ]{.ar} is irregular in that its 
;first; ;person; singular for the
;mudarie; verb
([I imagine]{.trans})
is more commonly
[**إِ**خَالُ]{.ar}
[**Ei**xAlu]{.trn}
instead of
[**أَ**خَالُ]{.ar}
[**Ea**xAlu]{.trn}.
For example,

(@) [إِخَالُ زَيْدًا أَخَاكَ]{.ar}
    [@wright@ 2/49C]{.citex}  
    [I imagine Zayd to be your brother.]{.trans}  

Here are some examples of [خَالَ]{.ar} as a ;fi3l_qalb;:

(@) [فَأُتِيَ بِكُرْسِيٍّ خِلْتُ قَوَائِمَهُ حَدِيدًا]{.ar}
    [@https://sunnah.com/nasai:5377@]{.citex}
    [Then he was brought a chair, whose legs I imagined to be of iron.]{.trans}  

(@) [مَا إِخَالُ أَحَدًا يَعْقِلُ يَرْمِي حَتَّى تَطْلُعَ الشَّمْسُ]{.ar}
    [@https://hadithunlocked.com/ahmad:2082@]{.citex}  
    [I don't imagine anyone of sense to stone until the sun rises.]{.trans}  
    (The first ;mafulb; is [أَحَدًا]{.trans}. And the second ;mafulb; is the ;j_f3l; [يَرْمِي]{.ar}.)  

### [زَعَمَ]{.ar}

[زَعَمَ]{.ar} means [to claim]{.trans}.


### [دَرَى]{.ar}

Usually used only with ;anna;.^[@radiy_kafiyah@ claims it is only used with ;anna;]
Examples:

Rarely, it can take two ;mafulb;s directly.
For example:

[@howell@ 2/135]{.citex}

### [تَعَلَّمْ]{.ar}

;ghair_mutasarrif;

Usually used only with ;anna;.^[@radiy_kafiyah@ claims it is only used with ;anna;]
Examples:

Rarely, it can take two ;mafulb;s directly.
For example:

[@howell@ 2/135]{.citex}

### [هَبْ]{.ar}

;ghair_mutasarrif;

### [سَمِعَ]{.ar}

[سَمِعَ]{.ar}
is, by default, a sensory verb
that means
[to hear]{.trans}.
And,
as such,
it takes one ;mafulb;.
For example:

(@) [سَمِعْتُ زَيْدًا]{.ar}  
    [I heard Zayd.]{.trans}

(@) [سَمِعْتُ صَوْتًا]{.ar}  
    [I heard a sound.]{.trans}

But,
as a special case,
[سَمِعَ]{.ar}
can take two ;mafulb;s
when the ;faa3il;
hears someone to be doing something.
For example:

(@) [سَمِعْتُ زَيْدٌ قَارِئًا]{.ar}
    [[@baseet_ibn_abi_rabee3@ 446](https://archive.org/details/0969pdf_201912/page/n445/mode/1up)]{.citex}  
    [I heard Zayd reading.]{.trans}  
    (The second ;mafulb; is the noun [قَارِئًا]{.ar}.)  

(@) [سَمِعْتُ زَيْدٌ يَقْرَأُ]{.ar}
    [[@howell@ §445 2/165](https://adamiturabi.github.io/howell-navigator/content/2-07-0.html?page=226)]{.citex}  
    [I heard Zayd reading.]{.trans}  
    (The second ;mafulb; is the ;j_f3l; [يَقْرَأُ]{.ar}.)  

In these examples,
[قَارِئًا]{.ar}
and
[يَقْرَأُ]{.ar}
are not considered a ;haal;
(as [ضَاحِكًا]{.ar} was considered a ;haal;
in example () [رَأَيْتُ زَيْدًا ضَاحِكًا]{.ar}
[I saw Zayd laughing.]{.trans}).
This is because the sentence,
in this context, would not be ;isnaad_comp; if you did not add
the second ;mafulb;.
That is, if, in this context, you said
[سَمِعْتُ زَيْدٌ]{.ar}
and stopped,
the listener would be left wondering, "You heard Zayd doing what?"
So a second ;mafulb; has to be added which gives the action that Zayd was doing which produced a sound.^[@https://tafsir.app/aldur-almasoon/21/60@]
Similarly,

(@) [قَالُوا۟ **سَمِعۡنَا فَتࣰى یَذۡكُرُهُمۡ** یُقَالُ لَهُۥۤ إِبۡرَ ٰ⁠هِیمُ]{.quran}
    [@https://quran.com/21/60@]{.citex}  
    [They said, "**We heard a young man mention them** who is called Abraham."]{.trans}  
    ([يَذْكُرُهُمْ]{.ar} is analyzed to be the second ;mafulb; of [سَمِعَ]{.ar}.^[@https://tafsir.app/aldur-almasoon/21/60@])

## The second ;mafulb; can be a sentence or phrase

Because ;af3aal_quloob; ;3amil;
what was originally a ;mubtada;-;xabar; sentence,
the first ;mafulb; may be anything which is allowed to be a ;mubtada;,
and
the second ;mafulb; may be anything which is allowed to be a ;xabar;.
Thus, the second ;mafulb;
may be a complete sentence in the ;mahall; ;acase;,
or an adverbial or prepositional phrase.^[[@baseet_ibn_abi_rabee3 443](https://archive.org/details/0969pdf_201912/page/n441/mode/2up)]

Here are some examples
where the second ;mafulb; is a complete sentence:

(@) [**مَا عَلِمْتُ رَسُولَ اللَّهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم نَكَحَ** شَيْئًا مِنْ نِسَائِهِ وَلاَ أَنْكَحَ شَيْئًا مِنْ بَنَاتِهِ عَلَى أَكْثَرَ مِنْ ثِنْتَىْ عَشْرَةَ أُوقِيَّةً]{.ar}
    [@https://sunnah.com/tirmidhi:1114b@]{.citex}  
    [**I did not know the Messenger of ;Allah; ;pbuh; to marry** any of his women, nor to give any of his daughters in marriage, for more than twelve [#Uqiyah]{.trn2}s.]{.trans}  
    (First ;mafulb; is [رَسُول الله]{.ar} [the Messenger of ;Allah;]{.trans}, second ;mafulb; is [نَكَحَ]{.ar} [he married]{.trans}.)

(@) [**مَا عَلِمْتُهُ صَامَ** شَهْرًا كُلَّهُ إِلاَّ رَمَضَانَ]{.ar}
    [@https://sunnah.com/muslim:1156b@]{.citex}  
    [**I did not know him to fast** any complete month except [#ramaDAn]{.trn2}.]{.trans}  
    (First ;mafulb; is [هُ]{.ar} [him]{.trans}, second ;mafulb; is [صَامَ]{.ar} [he fasted]{.trans}.)

(@) [**ظَنَنْتُهُ يَدْعُو** فِي الِاسْتِسْقَاءِ]{.ar}
    [@https://hadithunlocked.com/ibnkhuzaymah:1595@]{.citex}
    [**I thought him to be supplicating** in the rain prayer.]{.trans}  
    (First ;mafulb; is [هُ]{.ar} [him]{.trans}, second ;mafulb; is [يَدْعُو]{.ar} [supplicating]{.trans}.)

Here is an example
where the second ;mafulb; is a prepositional phrase:

(@) [قَالَ أَمَا وَاللَّهِ إِنَّ ذَلِكَ لِتَغَيُّرِ ثَائِرَةٍ كَانَتْ مِنِّي إِلَيْهِمْ وَلَكِنِّي **أَرَاهُمْ عَلَى ضَلَالَةٍ**]{.ar}
    [@https://hadithunlocked.com/hakim:4956@]{.citex}  
    [He said, "By ;Allah;, indeed that is because of a change in a matter between me and them, but **I think them to be on misguidance**."]{.trans}  
    (First ;mafulb; is [هُمْ]{.ar} [them]{.trans}, second ;mafulb; is [عَلَى ضَلَالٍ]{.ar} [on misguidance]{.trans}.)

## The first ;mafulb; may be a ;damir_shan;

Just like the second ;mafulb; may be a complete sentence,
similarly,
the first ;mafulb; may be a ;damir_shan;
because a ;damir_shan; can regularly be the ;mubtada; of a ;j_ism;.
So we can say:

(@) [حَسِبْتُ يَقُولُ زَيْدٌ]{.ar}
    [[@radiy_kafiyah@ 3/152](https://ketabonline.com/ar/books/23090/read?page=1587&part=4#p-23090-1587-2)]{.citex}  
    [I deemed [the state-of-affairs to be] Zayd is saying.]{.trans}

In example () above,
the first ;mafulb; of [حَسِبَ]{.ar}
is a ;mahzoof; ;damir_shan;,
as if to say:
[حَسِبْتُهُ يَقُولُ زَيْدٌ]{.ar}.^[[@radiy_kafiyah@ 3/152](https://ketabonline.com/ar/books/23090/read?page=1587&part=4#p-23090-1587-2)]

However, such usage will be rare.^[footnote]

## #;af3aal_quloob; with only one ;mafulb;

So far we have focused on
;af3aal_quloob;
that take two ;mafulb;s.
There are other
;af3aal_quloob;
that take only one ;mafulb;,
or no ;mafulb;.
They are not so much the subject of this chapter,
except that they can undertake a phenomenon called
_;ta3leeq;_ that we will study in @sec-ta3leeq below.
In any case, we give examples of some of these verbs:

[Examples of [عَرَفَ، تَفَكَّرَ]{.ar}]


Some of the ;af3aal_quloob; that can take two ;mafulb;s,
while keeping their meaning as
;af3aal_quloob;,
can take only one ;mafulb;.
[عَلِمَ]{.ar}
is the prime example of this variation.
For example,
we may say:

(@) [عَلِمْتُ زَيْدًا]{.ar}
    [@radiy_kafiyah_imam@ 2/988]{.citex}  
    [I knew Zayd.]{.trans}  

(@) [عَلِمْتُ خُرُوجَ زَيْدٍ]{.ar}
    [@radiy_kafiyah_imam@ 2/988]{.citex}  
    [I knew Zayd's going out.]{.trans}  

Similarly:

(@) [وَٱللَّهُ أَخۡرَجَكُم مِّنۢ بُطُونِ أُمَّهَـٰتِكُمۡ **لَا تَعۡلَمُونَ شَیۡـࣰٔا**]{.quran}
    [@https://quran.com/16/78@ cited by @nahw_arabi@ 1/236]{.citex}  
    [And Allāh has extracted you from the wombs of your mothers **not knowing a thing**]{.trans}  

(@) [لَقَدْ **عَلِمْتُ النَّظَائِرَ** الَّتِي كَانَ رَسُولُ اللَّهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم يَقْرَأُ بِهِنَّ سُورَتَيْنِ فِي رَكْعَةٍ]{.ar}
    [@https://sunnah.com/muslim:822e@]{.citex}  
    [**I know the manners** in which the Messenger of ;Allah; ;pbuh; recited two ;surah;s in one [rakeah]{.trn2}.]{.trans}  


Other ;af3aal_quloob;,
like ;dhanna;
usually require two ;mafulb;s.^[@radiy_kafiyah_imam@ 2/988]
Even so,
sometimes they may take only one ;mafulb;
when that ;mafulb; refers to
the thought being perceived.
This is because, as we discussed in section () above, 
even when the ;fi3l_qalb; takes two ;mafulb;s,
their ;taqdir; is a single ;mafulb;.^[[@radiy_kafiyah@ 4/153](https://ketabonline.com/ar/books/23090/read?page=1588&part=4#p-23090-1588-1)]
Here is an example of ;dhanna; with one ;mafulb;:

(@) [وَلَقَدْ نَزَلْتِ فَلَا **تَظُنِّي غَيْرَهُ** مِنِّي بِمَنْزِلَةً الْمُحَبِّ الْمُكْرَمِ]{.ar}
    [@radiy_kafiyah_imam@ 2/988]{.citex}  
    [And surely you have alighted, so don't **assume other than it** from me, in the place of alighting of the honored beloved.]{.trans}  

;dhanna; in example () above has only one ;mafulb; [غَيْرَهُ]{.ar}.
Similarly, the single ;mafulb; of ;dhanna;
can be a pronoun or ;ism_isharah; referring to the 
the thought being perceived.
For example:

(@) [ظَنَنْتُ ذَاكَ]{.ar}
    [[@sibawayhi@ 3/120](https://shamela.ws/book/23018/973)]{.citex}  
    [I thought that.]{.trans}  

In example () above,
[ذَاكَ]{.ar} can be the single ;mafulb; of ;dhanna;,
that refers to some thought.^[@radiy_kafiyah@ citing [الفراء]{.ar}]
The reason why [ذَاكَ]{.ar}
can be a ;mafulb;, and not necessarily refer to the ;masdar; as a ;mmutlaq;
(as we will see shortly),
is because one can add the ;masdar; separately as the ;mmutlaq;.
For example:

(@) [خِلْتُ ذَاكَ إِخَالُـ**ـهُ خَالًا**]{.ar}
    [[@ibn_malik_sharh_tasheel@ 2/65](https://shamela.ws/book/13257/471)]{.citex}  
    [I imagined that, imagining **it [with] an imagining**.]{.trans}  
    ([خَالًا]{.ar} is the ;mmutlaq; while [إِخَالُهُ]{.ar} is taking the pronoun [هُ]{.ar} as a ;mafulb;.)

Similarly, if someone says:

(@) [أَظُنُّ زَيْدًا قَائِمًا]{.ar}
    [@radiy_kafiyah@]{.citex}  
    [I assume Zayd to be standing.]{.trans}

then the reply to this can be:

(@) [أَنَا أَيْضًا أَظُنُّـ**ـهُ**]{.ar}
    [@radiy_kafiyah@]{.citex}  
    [I too assume **it**.]{.trans}  
    (The pronoun [هُ]{.ar} is a ;mafulb; and refers to the thought "Zayd is standing".)

Having said this,
some grammarians were of the opinion that
a single pronoun or ;ism_isharah; ;3amil;ed by ;dhanna; can only
refer to the ;masdar; of ;dhanna;,
such that it is a ;naib;
to the ;masdar; as the ;mmutlaq;.^[See [@abu_hayyan_tadhyeel@ 6/19](https://shamela.ws/book/17116/1710)]

;dhanna; can also occur with an indirect ;maful;,
which signifies the thing being thought _about_.
For example:

(@) [ظَنَنْتُ **بِهِ**]{.ar}
    [[@radiy_kafiyah@ 4/153](https://ketabonline.com/ar/books/23090/read?page=1588&part=4#p-23090-1588-2)]{.citex}  
    [I thought **about him**.]{.trans}  


Consider also the following ;ayah;:

(@) [وَطَاۤىِٕفَةࣱ قَدۡ أَهَمَّتۡهُمۡ أَنفُسُهُمۡ **یَظُنُّونَ بِٱللَّهِ غَیۡرَ ٱلۡحَقِّ ظَنَّ ٱلۡجَـٰهِلِیَّةِۖ**]{.quran}  
    [@https://quran.com/3/154@ cited by [@radiy_kafiyah@ 4/153](https://ketabonline.com/ar/books/23090/read?page=1588&part=4#p-23090-1588-2)]{.citex}  
    [while another faction worried about themselves, thinking of Allāh other than the truth - the thought of ignorance]{.trans}

There are a few different analyses of ;dhanna; and its
;ma3mul;s:

  i. [غَيْرَ الْحَقِّ]{.ar} is the ;mafulb; and [بِاللهِ]{.ar} is indicating who is being thought about,^[[@radiy_kafiyah@ 4/153](https://ketabonline.com/ar/books/23090/read?page=1588&part=4#p-23090-1588-2)] like:
     (@) [ظَنَنْتُ بِزَيْدٍ]{.ar}
         [@https://tafsir.app/aldur-almasoon/3/154@]{.citex}  
         [I thought about Zayd]{.trans}

 ii. [غَيْرَ الْحَقِّ]{.ar} is the first ;mafulb; and [بِاللهِ]{.ar} is the second ;mafulb;.^[[@3akbari_tibyan@ 1/303](https://shamela.ws/book/22928/304)]
iii. [غَيْرَ الْحَقِّ]{.ar} is the a ;naib; to the ;masdar; as a ;mmutlaq;, and [ظَنَّ الْجَاهِلِيَّةِ]{.ar} is its ;badal;.^[@https://tafsir.app/kashaf/3/154@]

## Suppressing one or both ;mafulb;s

Non-;af3aal_quloob;
that can take two ;mafulb;s
may sometimes take
only one ;mafulb;.
So, for example, instead of saying:

(@) [أَعْطَيْتُ زَيْدًا دِرْهَمًا]{.ar}  
    [I gave Zayd a dirham.]{.trans}

we can say both:

(@) [أَعْطَيْتُ دِرْهَمًا]{.ar}  
    [[@howell@ §443 2/152](https://adamiturabi.github.io/howell-navigator/content/2-07-0.html?page=213)]{.citex}  
    [I gave a dirham.]{.trans}

(@) [أَعْطَيْتُ زَيْدًا]{.ar}  
    [[@howell@ §443 2/152](https://adamiturabi.github.io/howell-navigator/content/2-07-0.html?page=213)]{.citex}  
    [I gave Zayd.]{.trans}

#;af3aal_quloob;,
;otoh;,
generally need both ;mafulb;s.
So, for example, instead of saying:

(@) [ظَنَنْتُ زَيْدًا قَائِمًا]{.ar}
    [[@howell@ §443 2/154](https://adamiturabi.github.io/howell-navigator/content/2-07-0.html?page=215)]{.citex}  
    [I thought Zayd to be standing.]{.trans}

we cannot say (without context):

(@) ;x; [ظَنَنْتُ زَيْدًا]{.ar}
    [[@howell@ §443 2/154](https://adamiturabi.github.io/howell-navigator/content/2-07-0.html?page=215)]{.citex}

(@) ;x; [ظَنَنْتُ قَائِمًا]{.ar}
    [[@howell@ §443 2/154](https://adamiturabi.github.io/howell-navigator/content/2-07-0.html?page=215)]{.citex}

However, it is possible to omit one of the two ;mafulb;s
if its meaning is implied and is indicated by context.^[[@howell@ §443 2/153](https://adamiturabi.github.io/howell-navigator/content/2-07-0.html?page=214)]
For example,

(@) [وَلَا **یَحۡسَبَنَّ** ٱلَّذِینَ یَبۡخَلُونَ بِمَاۤ ءَاتَىٰهُمُ ٱللَّهُ مِن فَضۡلِهِۦ **هُوَ خَیۡرࣰا لَّهُمۖ**]{.quran}
    [@https://quran.com/3/180@ cited by [@howell@ §443 2/153--154](https://adamiturabi.github.io/howell-navigator/content/2-07-0.html?page=214)^[cited as III. 175]]{.citex}  
    [And let not those who [greedily] withhold what Allāh has given them of His bounty **ever think that it is better for them**.]{.trans}

In the ;ayah; above,
the first ;mafulb; of
[يَحْسَبَنَّ]{.ar}
is interpreted
(in one interpretation of this reading)
to be a suppressed [بُخْلَهُمْ]{.ar}
[their miserliness]{.trans},
and [هُوَ]{.ar} is a ;damir_fasl;.
Such that the meaning is:

(@) [ولا يَحْسَبَنَّ الباخِلون **بُخْلَهم** هو خيرًا لهم]{.ar}
    [@https://tafsir.app/aldur-almasoon/3/180@]{.citex}  
    [And let not the misers think **their miserliness** to be good for them.]{.trans}

Both ;mafulb;s can also be omitted together.
For example:

<!--
(@) [وَظَنَنتُمۡ ظَنَّ ٱلسَّوۡءِ]{.quran}
    [@https://quran.com/48/12@ cited by [@howell@ §443 2/153](https://adamiturabi.github.io/howell-navigator/content/2-07-0.html?page=214)]{.citex}  
    [And you assumed an assumption of evil]{.trans}  
    ([ظَنَّ]{.ar} is analyzed to be a ;mmutlaq;.^[@https://tafsir.app/iraab-aldarweesh/48/12@])  

(@) [ظَنَنْتُ ذَاكَ]{.ar}
    [[@howell@ §443 2/154](https://adamiturabi.github.io/howell-navigator/content/2-07-0.html?page=215)]{.citex}  
    [I thought that.]{.trans}  
    ([ذَاكَ]{.ar} is a ;naib; to the ;masdar; as the ;mmutlaq;.^[But see also [@abu_hayyan_tadhyeel@ 6/19](https://shamela.ws/book/17116/1710)])
-->

(@) [مَنْ يَسْمَعْ يَخَلْ]{.ar}
    [[@howell@ §443 2/153](https://adamiturabi.github.io/howell-navigator/content/2-07-0.html?page=214)]{.citex}  
    [Whoso hears, will think.]{.trans}  

The preposition [بِ]{.ar} may be used with ;dhanna; to mean [about]{.trans}.
In this case as well, no ;mafulb; is needed.
For example:

(@) [ظَنَنْتُ بِهِ]{.ar}
    [[@howell@ §443 2/154](https://adamiturabi.github.io/howell-navigator/content/2-07-0.html?page=215)]{.citex}  
    [I thought about him.]{.trans}

Even in such cases where both ;mafulb;s are omitted,
their meaning may be implied.
For example:

(@) [وَیَوۡمَ یُنَادِیهِمۡ فَیَقُولُ أَیۡنَ شُرَكَاۤءِیَ ٱلَّذِینَ **كُنتُمۡ تَزۡعُمُونَ**]{.quran}
    [@https://quran.com/28/62@ cited by [@howell@ §443 2/153](https://adamiturabi.github.io/howell-navigator/content/2-07-0.html?page=214)]{.citex}  
    [And [warn of] the Day He will call them and say, "Where are My 'partners' which **you used to claim**?"]{.trans}  

In the ;ayah; above, the two suppressed ;mafulb;s of [تَزْعُمُونَ]{.ar}
are interpreted to be thus:

(@) [تَزْعُمُونَهُمْ شُرَكَاءَ]{.ar}
    [[@howell@ §443 2/153](https://adamiturabi.github.io/howell-navigator/content/2-07-0.html?page=214)]{.citex}  
    [...\ you claim them to be partners]{.trans}

Suppressing one or both ;mafulb;s in the answer to a question is especially common.
For example, in response to the question:

(@) [أتظن زيدًا قائما]{.ar}
    [[@shatibi_sharf_alfiyyah@ 2/495](https://shamela.ws/book/20562/1156)]{.citex}  
    [Do you think Zayd to be standing?]{.trans}

All three of the following replies are acceptable:

(@) [ظننت زيدًا]{.ar}
    [[@shatibi_sharf_alfiyyah@ 2/495](https://shamela.ws/book/20562/1156)]{.citex}  
    [I think Zayd [to be standing].]{.trans}

(@) [ظننتُ قائمًا]{.ar}
    [[@shatibi_sharf_alfiyyah@ 2/495](https://shamela.ws/book/20562/1156)]{.citex}  
    [I think [Zayd to be] standing.]{.trans}

(@) [ظننت]{.ar}
    [[@shatibi_sharf_alfiyyah@ 2/495](https://shamela.ws/book/20562/1156)]{.citex}  
    [I think [Zayd to be standing].]{.trans}

Similarly:

(@) [قُلْتُ صَلَّاهَا النَّبِيُّ ﷺ  قَالَ لَا إِخَالُ]{.ar}
    [@https://hadithunlocked.com/ibnabishaybah:7856@]{.citex}  
    [I said, "Did the Prophet ;pbuh; pray it?" He said, "I don't think so."]{.trans}  

## #;ta3leeq; of government {#sec-ta3leeq}

Sometimes,
there can be a sentence where a
;fi3l_qalb;
does not take its ;mafulb;(s)
directly.
Instead its
direct ;3amal;
is _;mu3allaq;_ due to the presence of a _;mu3alliq;_.
This phenomenon is called
_;ta3leeq;_ of government.
Let's take a look at an example.
Consider a sentence where ;dhanna; exercises it ;3amiling; effect.

(@) [ظَنَنْتُ زَيْدًا قَائِمًا]{.ar}
    [I thought Zayd to be standing.]{.trans}  

Now let's see what happens when the
original
;mubtada;
([زَيْد]{.ar})
and ;xabar;
([قَائِم]{.ar})
are preceded by a ;laam_ibt;.
The sentence becomes:

(@) [ظَنَنْتُ لَزَيْدٌ قَائِمٌ]{.ar}
    [[@howell@ §445 2/158](https://adamiturabi.github.io/howell-navigator/content/2-07-0.html?page=219)]{.citex}  
    [I thought, assuredly Zayd is standing.]{.trans}  

As you can see,
the
original
;mubtada;
([زَيْد]{.ar})
and ;xabar;
([قَائِم]{.ar})
are now both in the ;ucase;.
This is because the effect of the ;laam_ibt;
is to cause a
;mubtada;
and ;xabar;
to be in the ;ucase;.
The ;3amal; of ;dhanna; is thus ;mu3allaq;.
The inner sentence
[لَزَيْدٌ قَائِمٌ]{.ar}
is said to be in the ;mahall; ;acase;
as a ;mafulb; of ;dhanna; that ;sadd_masadd; of two ;mafulb;s.

The proof that the inner sentence
[لَزَيْدٌ قَائِمٌ]{.ar}
is in the ;mahall; ;acase;
and that the ;3amal; of ;dhanna; is ;mu3allaq;,
is that if we were to put a ;3atf; after this sentence,
then the ;3amiling; effect of ;dhanna; would resume.
For example:

(@) [ظَنَنْتُ لَزَيْدٌ قَائِمٌ **وَعَمْرًا مُنْطَلِقًا**]{.ar}
    [[@howell@ §445 2/158](https://adamiturabi.github.io/howell-navigator/content/2-07-0.html?page=219)]{.citex}  
    [I thought, assuredly Zayd is standing **and ;3amr; is setting out**.]{.trans}  

The ;mu3alliq;s that ;yu3alliq; the ;3amal; of
the ;af3aal_quloob; are discussed in the subsections below:

### The negaters ;maa;, ;in;, and ;laa;

Examples:

(@) [لَقَدۡ عَلِمۡتَ مَا هَـٰۤؤُلَاۤءِ یَنطِقُونَ]{.quran}
    [@https://quran.com/21/65@ cited by @nahw_arabi@ 1/346; [@howell@ §445 2/160](https://adamiturabi.github.io/howell-navigator/content/2-07-0.html?page=221)]{.citex}  
    ["You have already known that these do not speak!"]{.trans}  

In example () above, the negater ;maa; prevents [عَلِمْتَ]{.ar} from
directly ;3amiling; two ;mafulb;s. Instead,
the sentence
[مَا هَؤُلَاءِ يَنْطِقُونَ]{.ar}
is in the ;mahall; ;acase; as a ;mafulb;
that ;sadd_masadd; two ;mafulb;s.
Similarly:

(@) [عَلِمْتُ وَاللهِ إِنْ زَيْدٌ قَائِمٌ]{.ar}
    [[@howell@ §445 2/160](https://adamiturabi.github.io/howell-navigator/content/2-07-0.html?page=221)]{.citex}  
    [I knew, by ;Allah;, Zayd is not standing.]{.trans}  

(@) [یَوۡمَ یَدۡعُوكُمۡ فَتَسۡتَجِیبُونَ بِحَمۡدِهِۦ وَتَظُنُّونَ إِن لَّبِثۡتُمۡ إِلَّا قَلِیلࣰا]{.quran}
    [@https://quran.com/17/52@ cited by [@howell@ §445 2/160](https://adamiturabi.github.io/howell-navigator/content/2-07-0.html?page=221)]{.citex}  
    [On the Day He will call you and you will respond with praise of Him and think that you had not remained [in the world] except for a little."]{.trans}  

(@) [عَلِمْتُ وَاللهِ لَا زَيْدٌ فِي الدَّارِ ولَا عَمْرٌو]{.ar}
    [[@howell@ §445 2/160](https://adamiturabi.github.io/howell-navigator/content/2-07-0.html?page=221)]{.citex}  
    [I knew, by ;Allah;, Zayd is not in the house, nor ;3amr;.]{.trans}  


### ;laam_ibt;

We have already seen in example () above, how ;laam_ibt; ;yu3alliq;s
the direct ;3amal; of a ;fi3l_qalb;.
Here is another example:

(@) [وَلَقَدۡ **عَلِمُوا۟ لَمَنِ** ٱشۡتَرَىٰهُ مَا لَهُۥ فِی ٱلۡـَٔاخِرَةِ مِنۡ خَلَـٰقࣲۚ]{.quran}
    [@https://quran.com/2/102@ cited by [@howell@ §445 2/160](https://adamiturabi.github.io/howell-navigator/content/2-07-0.html?page=221)]{.citex}  
    [But **they [i.e., the Children of Israel] certainly knew that whoever** purchased it [i.e., magic] would not have in the Hereafter any share.]{.trans}  


### ;laam_qasam;

(@) [لَقدْ عَلِمْتُ لَتَأْتِيَنَّ مَنِيَّتِي ~ إِنَّ الْمَنَايًا لَا تَطِيشُ سِهَامُهَا]{.ar}
    [@nahw_arabi@ 1/346; [@howell@ §445 2/158](https://adamiturabi.github.io/howell-navigator/content/2-07-0.html?page=219)]{.citex}  
    [And assuredly, I have known (by God) verily my fate will come. Verily the fates---their arrows do not miss.]{.trans}  

The presence of the ;laam_qasam; in 
[لَتَأْتِيَنَّ]{.ar}
;yu3alliq;s the direct ;3amal; of [عَلِمْتُ]{.ar}.
Otherwise the sentence would have been:

(@) [عَلِمْتُ مَنِيَّتِي آتِيَةً]{.ar}
    [@nahw_arabi@ 1/436]{.citex}  
    [I have known my fate to be coming.]{.trans}  

### A ;istifham; sentence

A ;istifham; sentence can follow
a ;fi3l_qalb;
and in such a case
the ;3amal; of the ;fi3l_qalb;
is ;mu3allaq;
if the entire ;istifham; sentence
is its ;mafulb;.

Here is an example:

(@) [عَلِمْتُ أَزَيْدٌ فِي الدَّارِ أَمْ عَمْرٌو]{.ar}
    [[@howell@ §445 2/159](https://adamiturabi.github.io/howell-navigator/content/2-07-0.html?page=220)]{.citex}  
    [I knew whether Zayd was in the house or ;3amr;.]{.trans}  

In example () above,
the entire ;istifham; sentence
[أَزَيْدٌ فِي الدَّارِ أَمْ عَمْرٌو]{.ar}
is in the ;acase;
and it ;sadd_masadd; the two ;mafulb;s of [عَلِمْتُ]{.ar}.
That is the traditional explanation.
However, it is also possible that
[عَلِمَ]{.ar} here requires only one ;mafulb;.
In which case the ;istifham; sentence
;sadd_masadd; the one required ;mafulb;.

Another point to note is that the ;istifham; sentence
is now no longer a question to the listener.
That is why we have not puntuated the translation with a question mark (?).
Rather, the entire example sentence
is signifying that the speaker knows the answer to the question.

Here is another example:

(@) [وَلَتَعۡلَمُنَّ أَیُّنَاۤ أَشَدُّ عَذَابࣰا وَأَبۡقَىٰ]{.quran}
    [@https://quran.com/20/71@ cited by [@howell@ §445 2/159](https://adamiturabi.github.io/howell-navigator/content/2-07-0.html?page=220)]{.citex}  
    [and you will surely know which of us is more severe in [giving] punishment and more enduring]{.trans}

In example () above,
there are three possible interpretations^[@https://tafsir.app/aldur-almasoon/20/71@]:

a. The first interpretation, and the one relevant to our discussion here,
   is that ;ayy; is a ;mubtada; and [أَشَدّ]{.ar} is its ;xabar;.
   The ;istifham; sentence
   [أَیُّنَا أَشَدُّ عَذَابًا وَأَبْقَىٰ]{.ar}
   ;sadd_masadd; the two ;mafulb;s of [تَعْلَمُنَّ]{.ar}.
b. Another interpretation is [تَعْلَمُنَّ]{.ar} here only requires one ;mafulb;
   and the ;istifham; sentence is that (;mahall;) ;mafulb;.
c. A third interpretation is that [أَيّ]{.ar} is a ;ism_mawsul;.
   ;ayy; itself (not the entire ;istifham; sentence) is the ;mafulb; of
   [تَعْلَمُنَّ]{.ar}.
   And ;ayy; is ;mabny; ending with a ;umark; because of a phenomenon described in @sec-mabny_ayy.

Here are some more examples:

(@) [عَلِمْتُ مَتَىٰ السَّفَرُ]{.ar}
    [[@howell@ §445 2/159](https://adamiturabi.github.io/howell-navigator/content/2-07-0.html?page=220)]{.citex}  
    [I knew when the journey was (or would be).]{.trans}

(@) [عَلِمْتُ أَبُو مَنْ زَيْدٌ]{.ar}
    [[@howell@ §445 2/159](https://adamiturabi.github.io/howell-navigator/content/2-07-0.html?page=220)]{.citex}  
    [I knew whose father was Zayd.]{.trans}

(@) [عَلِمْتُ صَبِيحَةَ أَيِّ يَوْمٍ سَفَرُكَ]{.ar}
    [[@howell@ §445 2/159](https://adamiturabi.github.io/howell-navigator/content/2-07-0.html?page=220)]{.citex}  
    [I knew the morning of which day your journey was (or will be).]{.trans}

(@) [وَسَیَعۡلَمُ ٱلَّذِینَ ظَلَمُوۤا۟ أَیَّ مُنقَلَبࣲ یَنقَلِبُونَ]{.quran}
    [@https://quran.com/26/227@ cited by [@howell@ §445 2/159](https://adamiturabi.github.io/howell-navigator/content/2-07-0.html?page=220)]{.citex}  
    [And those who have wronged are going to know to what [kind of] return they will be returned.]{.trans}  

In example () above, ;ayy; is a ;adat_istifham; in the ;acase; as a ;mmutlaq;, ;3amiled; by [يَنْقَلِبُونَ]{.ar}.^[@https://tafsir.app/aldur-almasoon/26/227@]
The entire ;istifham; sentence is in the ;acase; ;3amiled; by [سَيَعْلَمُ]{.ar}.

### Other ;mu3alliq;s of ;3amal;

There are other, less common, ;mu3alliq;s
discussed by the grammarians.
We will list some of them below:

#### ;la3alla; {.unnumbered}

Example:

(@) [وَإِنۡ أَدۡرِی **لَعَلَّهُۥ** فِتۡنَةࣱ لَّكُمۡ وَمَتَـٰعٌ إِلَىٰ حِینࣲ]{.quran}
    [@https://quran.com/21/111@ cited by [@howell@ §445 2/160](https://adamiturabi.github.io/howell-navigator/content/2-07-0.html?page=221)]{.citex}  
    [And I know not; **perhaps** it is a trial for you and enjoyment for a time."]{.trans}  

#### The ;adat_shart; ;law; {.unnumbered}

For example:

(@) [وَلَقَدْ عَلِمَ الْأَقْوَامُ **لَوْ** أَنَّ حَاتِمًا ~ أَرَادَ ثَرَاءَ الْمَالِ كَانَ لَهُ وَفْرٌ]{.ar}
    [[@howell@ §445 2/160](https://adamiturabi.github.io/howell-navigator/content/2-07-0.html?page=221)]{.citex}  
    [And the peoples have known that had [#HAtim]{.trn2} desired abundance of property, he would have had affluence.]{.trans}  

#### ;inna; that has a ;laam_frq;

Example:

(@) [عَلِمْتُ إِنَّ زَيْدًا لَقَائِمٌ]{.ar}
    [[@howell@ §445 2/161](https://adamiturabi.github.io/howell-navigator/content/2-07-0.html?page=222)]{.citex}  
    [I knew: indeed Zayd is standing.]{.trans}  

### The verbs whose ;3amal; may be ;mu3allaq;

#;ta3leeq; of ;3amal; is possible for the following categories of verbs:

#### The ;mutasarrif; ;af3aal_quloob; that take two ;mafulb;s {.unnumbered}

We have seen examples of ;ta3leeq; with ;af3aal_quloob; that take two ;mafulb;s like ;dhanna;, [عَلِمَ]{.ar}, [حَسِبَ]{.ar}, etc.
above.

;af3aal_quloob; that are ;ghair_mutasarrif;
like
[هَبْ]{.ar} [grant]{.trans}
and
[تَعَلَّمْ]{.ar} [learn]{.trans},
which are only used in the ;fi3l_amr;,
are excluded from having their ;3amal; ;mu3allaq;.

The ;af3aal_tasyeer;,
like
[صَيَّرَ]{.ar} [to make _x_ become _y_]{.trans}
[تَرَكَ]{.ar} [to leave _x_ as _y_]{.trans},
etc.,
are also excluded.

#### Any other ;fi3l_qalb; even if it does not take two ;mafulb;s {.unnumbered}

Some ;af3aal_quloob; may take only one ;mafulb;, like
[عَرَفَ]{.ar} [to recognize, know]{.trans}.
These too are subject to ;ta3leeq;.
So, for example, we can say:

(@) [عَرَفْتُ مَنْ أَبُوكَ]{.ar}
    [[@howell@ §445 2/164](https://adamiturabi.github.io/howell-navigator/content/2-07-0.html?page=225)]{.citex}  
    [I knew who your father is/was.]{.trans}  

In example () above,
[عَرَفْتُ]{.ar} would have taken a noun as a ;mafulb;,
but the ;adat_istifham; ;yu3alliq;s its ;3amal;
and so the entire ;istifham; sentence
[مَنْ أَبُوكَ]{.ar}
;sadd_masadd; of its ;mafulb;.

Other ;af3aal_quloob; that take only only one ;mafulb;
(like [عَلِمَ]{.ar} when used to mean [to know]{.trans}),
or that take an indirect ;mafulb; 
(like [تَفَكَّرَ فِي]{.ar} [to think about]{.trans}),
are also similarly subject to ;ta3leeq;.^[[@howell@ §445 2/164](https://adamiturabi.github.io/howell-navigator/content/2-07-0.html?page=225)]

#### Verbs which can enable the ;af3aal_quloob; {.unnumbered}

There are some verbs that are not ;af3aal_quloob; per se,
but they can enable
the ;af3aal_quloob;.
These verbs too may be subject to ;ta3leeq;.^[[@baseet_ibn_abi_rabee3@ 446](https://archive.org/details/0969pdf_201912/page/n445/mode/2up)]
Let's explain what we mean with some examples.

<!--
The verb
[سَمِعَ]{.ar}
[to hear]{.trans}
is a sensory verb, not a ;fi3l_qalb;.
But hearing enables one to _know_.
[سَمِعَ]{.ar}
can even take two ;mafulb;s, for example:

(@) [سَمِعْتُ زَيْدٌ قَارِئًا]{.ar}
    [[@baseet_ibn_abi_rabee3@ 446](https://archive.org/details/0969pdf_201912/page/n445/mode/1up)]{.citex}  
    [I heard Zayd reading.]{.trans}  

(@) [سَمِعْتُ زَيْدٌ يَقْرَأُ]{.ar}
    [[@howell@ §445 2/165](https://adamiturabi.github.io/howell-navigator/content/2-07-0.html?page=226)]{.citex}  
    [I heard Zayd reading.]{.trans}  
-->

The verb [رَأَى]{.ar} [to see]{.trans}
enables its ;faa3il; to _know_.
Therefore, it may be subject to ;ta3leeq; of ;3amal;.
For example:

(@) [أَمَا تَرَى أَيُّ بَرْقٍ هَـٰهُنَا]{.ar}
    [[@howell@ §445 2/165](https://adamiturabi.github.io/howell-navigator/content/2-07-0.html?page=226)]{.citex}  
    [Do you not see which [kind of] lightning is here?]{.trans}  

Similarly,
the verb [سَأَلَ]{.ar}
[to ask]{.trans}
enables one to know.
Therefore its ;3amal; can be ;mu3allaq;.
For example:

(@) [اسْأَلْ أَيُّهُمْ زَيْدٌ]{.ar}
    [[@baseet_ibn_abi_rabee3@ 446](https://archive.org/details/0969pdf_201912/page/n445/mode/1up)]{.citex}  
    [Ask which of them is Zayd]{.trans}

(@) [یَسۡـَٔلُونَ أَیَّانَ یَوۡمُ ٱلدِّینِ]{.quran}
    [@https://quran.com/51/12@ cited by @nahw_arabi@ 1/347]{.citex}  
    [They ask, "When is the Day of Recompense?"]{.trans}  

The same can be said of the verb
[نَظَرَ]{.ar} [to look]{.trans}.
Example:

(@) [فَلۡیَنظُرۡ أَیُّهَاۤ أَزۡكَىٰ طَعَامࣰا]{.quran}
    [@https://quran.com/18/19@ cited by @nahw_arabi@ 1/347]{.citex}  
    [and let him look to which is the best of food]{.trans}  
   
## #;ilghaa; of government

Similar to ;ta3leeq; is
is another phenomenon called _;ilghaa;_.
#;ilghaa;
occurs when a ;fi3l_qalb; exercises no ;3amal; at all.

Consider the following sentence:

(@) [ظَنَنْتُ زَيْدًا عَالِمًا]{.ar}
    [[@howell@ §444 2/155](https://adamiturabi.github.io/howell-navigator/content/2-07-0.html?page=216)]{.citex}  
    [I thought Zayd to be knowledgeable.]{.trans}  

In example () above,
;dhanna; is governing
the original ;mubtada; ([زَيْد]{.ar})
and original ;xabar; ([عَالِم]{.ar})
as usual.

If we move the position of the verb
(as is allowed),
then the 
the original ;mubtada; ([زَيْد]{.ar})
and original ;xabar; ([عَالِم]{.ar})
can remain ;mafulb;s.
So we can say:

(@) [زَيْدًا **ظَنَنْتُ** عَالِمًا]{.ar}
    [[@howell@ §444 2/155](https://adamiturabi.github.io/howell-navigator/content/2-07-0.html?page=216)]{.citex}  
    [Zayd **I thought** to be knowledgeable.]{.trans}  

(@) [زَيْدًا عَالِمً **اظَنَنْتُ**]{.ar}
    [[@howell@ §444 2/155](https://adamiturabi.github.io/howell-navigator/content/2-07-0.html?page=216)]{.citex}  
    [Zayd to be knowledgeable **I thought**.]{.trans}  

However, 
when the verb is moved from its initial position to an intervening or final position,
then its ;3amal; may optionally be _;mulghaa;_.
In that case,
[زَيْد]{.ar}
and
[عَالِم]{.ar}
stay as
the ;mubtada;
and ;xabar;,
in the ;ucase;.
So we can say:

(@) [زَيْدٌ **ظَنَنْتُ** عَالِمٌ]{.ar}
    [Zayd **I thought** to be knowledgeable.]{.trans}  

(@) [زَيْدٌ عَالِمٌ **اظَنَنْتُ**]{.ar}
    [[@howell@ §444 2/156](https://adamiturabi.github.io/howell-navigator/content/2-07-0.html?page=217)]{.citex}  
    [Zayd to be knowledgeable **I thought**.]{.trans}  


The difference between
;ilghaa;
and
;ta3leeq;
is that
;ta3leeq;
still ;3amil;s in meaning, if not in wording.
It's just that the ;mu3alliq;
introduces a new sentence that then ;sadd_masadd; the
;mafulb;s of the ;fi3l_qalb;.
Whereas, in the case of ;ilghaa;,
there is no ;3amal; of the ;fi3l_qalb;
whether in meaning or in wording.

The standard rule is that ;ilghaa; is only allowed
when the verb is in an intervening or final position,
as in examples () and () above.

When the verb is in an intervening position,
then both ;3amal; (example ())
and ;ilghaa; (example ())
are equally permissible.
And when the verb is in the final position,
then ;ilghaa; (example ()) is considered better,
while ;3amal; (example ()) is also permissible.^[[@howell@ §444 2/156](https://adamiturabi.github.io/howell-navigator/content/2-07-0.html?page=217)]

When the verb is in the initial position,
as in example () above,
then,
as we have already mentioned,
the standard rule is that
;ilghaa; is disallowed.^[[@howell@ §444 2/156](https://adamiturabi.github.io/howell-navigator/content/2-07-0.html?page=217)]
So the verb must govern the
the original ;mubtada;
and original ;xabar;
as ;mafulb;s.

However,
there are instances of a verb occurring in initial position while the
the original ;mubtada;
and original ;xabar;
remain in the ;ucase;.
These are then explained away using ;taqdir;.
For example:

(@) [أَرْجُو وَآمُلُ أَنْ بَدْنُو مَوَدَّتُهَا * وَمَا **إِخَالُ لَدَيْنَا مِنْكَ تَنْوِيلُ**]{.ar}
    [[@howell@ §444 2/156](https://adamiturabi.github.io/howell-navigator/content/2-07-0.html?page=217)]{.citex}  
    [I hope and faintly expect that her love may approach; but I fancy not a bestowal of favor from you to us.]{.trans}  

In example () above [تَنْوِيلُ]{.ar} is in the ;ucase;
while [إِخَالُ]{.ar} precedes it.
To reconcile this,
a ;mahzoof; ;damir_shan; is ;qaddared; as the first ;mafulb; of [إِخَالُ]{.ar}.
The second (;mahall;) ;mafulb; is then the following sentence.
The complete ;taqdir; is:

(@) [إِخَالُـ**ـهُ** لَدَيْنَا مِنْكَ تَنْوِيلُ]{.ar}

Similarly:

(@) [كَذَاكَ أُدِّبْتُ حَتَّى صَارَ مِنْ خُلُقِي * أَنِّي **وَجَدْتُ مِلَاكُ الشِّيمَةِ الْأَدَبُ**]{.ar}
    [[@howell@ §444 2/157](https://adamiturabi.github.io/howell-navigator/content/2-07-0.html?page=218)]{.citex}  
    [Thus was I trained to good behavior until it became [a part] of my nature, that I perceived the basis of character to be training.]{.trans}  

In example () above,
[مِلَاكُ]{.ar}
are
[الْأَدَبُ]{.ar}
are in the ;ucase;,
even though the verb [وَجَدْتُ]{.ar} precedes them.
To reconcile this,
a ;mahzoof; ;laam_ibt; is ;qaddared;, 
;yu3alliq;ing the ;3amal; of [وَجَدْتُ]{.ar}, thus:

(@) [وَجَدْتُ **لَـ**ـمِلَاكُ الشِّيمَةِ الْأَدَبُ]{.ar}

Some grammarians allowed ;ilghaa; even when the verb is in the initial position.
They then do not require ;taqdir; to explain the above verses.^[[@howell@ §444 2/157](https://adamiturabi.github.io/howell-navigator/content/2-07-0.html?page=218)]
